w: Acceleration and top speed over 5–20 m.

U9–U10: Noticeably slower than age peers; running action uncoordinated.
Keeps pace with most peers; reasonable running form.
First to loose balls against any opposition; quick off the mark and fast over distance.
U11–U13: Regularly beaten in races to the ball; slow first steps.
Competitive in most foot races; decent acceleration.
Outpaces almost anyone their age; explosive first steps and sustains top speed.

w: Holding their own in contact; shielding and competing physically.

U9–U10: Easily knocked over in contact; avoids challenges.
Holds their own in most contact for their age.
Very strong in contact for their age; hard to knock off the ball.
U11–U13: Easily knocked off the ball; avoids contact.
Holds their own in most duels; uses body to shield.
Dominates duels against the best of their age; very hard to move off the ball.

w: Keeping intensity through a session or match.

U9–U10: Tires early; often stops or walks during games.
Stays involved for most of the session with short dips.
High energy throughout; still making runs late on.
U11–U13: Intensity drops sharply after short spells.
Keeps work rate for most of a half; recovers between efforts.
Repeats high-intensity efforts all game and recovers quickly.

w: Changing direction at speed while staying balanced.

U9–U10: Loses balance or slows heavily when turning.
Turns and changes direction with control at moderate speed.
Sharp, balanced changes of direction at full speed.
U11–U13: Needs several steps to turn; heavy on the heels.
Efficient turns; lowers centre of gravity, stays in control.
Changes direction explosively and re-accelerates instantly.

w: Body shape and preparation to control the ball.

U9–U10: Struggles to stop or control passes coming to them.
Gets in line with the ball and controls most ground passes.
Controls ground and bouncing balls comfortably with different surfaces.
U11–U13: Receives square-on and static; struggles with balls in the air.
Opens body to receive; controls ground and most aerial balls.
Receives on the half-turn under pressure, any height, either foot.

w: Quality and direction of the first touch.

U9–U10: Ball often bounces away; needs several touches.
First touch keeps the ball close, ready for the next action.
First touch moves the ball into space away from pressure.
U11–U13: First touch often invites pressure.
Touch sets up the next action when given time.
Directional first touch under pressure; plays forward on the second touch.

w: Accuracy, weight and range of passing.

U9–U10: Passes often miss the target or lack weight; mostly toe-pokes.
Accurate short passes with the inside of the foot.
Accurate short and longer passes with good weight, including on the move.
U11–U13: Short passes often misplaced; limited range.
Reliable short and medium passing; adjusts weight.
Wide range, accurate under pressure; disguises and breaks lines consistently.

w: Technique and timing when heading the ball.

U9–U10: Avoids the ball in the air or uses the top of the head.
Uses the forehead with correct technique in light practices.
Confident, with good technique and timing for their age.
U11–U13: Avoids heading or uses the top of the head; poor timing.
Meets the ball with the forehead and good technique.
Attacks the ball, times jumps well and directs headers with purpose.

w: Striking technique, accuracy and composure in front of goal.

U9–U10: Rarely gets shots on target; frequent mis-kicks.
Strikes the ball cleanly and on target from close range.
Finishes with power and placement using different techniques.
U11–U13: Shots often off target or weak.
On target most of the time inside the box; picks a corner.
Composed finisher with either foot; varies placement, power and volleys.

w: Close control while moving and changing direction.

U9–U10: Ball gets away when moving; head always down.
Keeps the ball close while moving and changing direction.
Excellent close control with both feet and a range of moves.
U11–U13: Loses close control under any pressure.
Keeps close control in tight spaces with a reliable move.
Close control at speed in tight areas; several moves, both feet.

w: Covering ground at speed with the ball into space.

U9–U10: Ball runs away, or slows almost to a stop.
Runs into space with the ball under control.
Drives at speed into space and keeps control.
U11–U13: Loses control when increasing speed.
Carries the ball forward at pace; head up occasionally.
Drives at speed with head up; releases a pass or shot at the end of the run.

w: Delivering the ball into the box from wide areas.

U9–U10: Can't lift or play the ball into the box from wide.
Plays the ball into the box from wide with the stronger foot.
Picks out teammates in the box with different deliveries.
U11–U13: Crosses rarely beat the first defender.
Delivers a cross into the box from wide with the stronger foot.
Consistent quality delivery (driven, lofted, cut-back) chosen for the situation.

w: Timing and technique to win the ball cleanly.

U9–U10: Mistimed, or no attempt to win the ball.
Wins the ball with a clean block or poke tackle.
Wins the ball cleanly and comes away with it.
U11–U13: Mistimed challenges; frequent fouls.
Times tackles well in most situations.
Clean, well-timed tackles of different types; keeps possession after.

w: Trying and finding unexpected, effective solutions.

U9–U10: Always plays the same safe action; reluctant to try things.
Sometimes tries a trick or something unexpected.
Regularly invents solutions and surprises opponents.
U11–U13: Predictable; repeats one solution.
Varies actions; occasionally produces something unexpected that works.
Consistently unpredictable and effective in the right areas.

w: Width, depth, support, playing forward.

U9–U10: Bunches near the ball.
Spreads out to give width when the team has the ball.
Finds space and helps the team spread out without being told.
U11–U13: Rarely in a useful position; bunches near the ball.
Applies width, depth and support most of the time.
Consistently creates and uses space; helps teammates do it.

w: Scanning before receiving and seeing options.

U9–U10: Head down; doesn't look before receiving.
Sometimes looks up and sees a nearby teammate.
Often looks around before receiving; sees passes others miss.
U11–U13: Rarely scans before receiving.
Scans in open play; sees the obvious pass.
Scans constantly; sees and plays passes others don't.

w: Choosing when to pass, dribble or shoot.

U9–U10: Often loses the ball by forcing the same action.
Knows when to pass, dribble or shoot in simple situations.
Often makes the clever choice and plays with head up.
U11–U13: Often picks the wrong option.
Usually picks a sensible option.
Consistently picks the best option at the right moment.

w: Taking on and beating an opponent in games.

U9–U10: Avoids taking players on, or loses the ball immediately.
Tries to beat a defender when there's space.
Regularly beats defenders 1v1 in games.
U11–U13: Rarely attempts it, or loses the ball quickly.
Takes on opponents at the right moments with some success.
Match-winner in 1v1s; picks the right moment and area.

w: Carrying out positional duties when the team has the ball.

U9–U10: Unsure where to stand.
Knows their position's basic job when we have the ball.
Does their job and can play more than one position.
U11–U13: Unsure of role; drifts out of position.
Understands the main duties of their position.
Performs the role fully and adapts to more than one position.

w: Pressure, cover, balance, recovering behind the ball.

U9–U10: Stays where they are when the ball is lost.
Gets back behind the ball when we lose it.
Recovers quickly and helps teammates get organised.
U11–U13: Does not recover or track.
Understands pressure, cover and balance; recovers behind the ball.
Organises self and others; anticipates the team's defensive needs.

w: Spotting danger early and intercepting.

U9–U10: Only notices danger once it happens.
Sometimes steps in to intercept a simple pass.
Reads simple passes early and intercepts often.
U11–U13: Reacts late to danger.
Anticipates simple passes and sometimes intercepts.
Reads play early; regularly intercepts and cuts out passes.

w: Choosing when to press, delay or cover.

U9–U10: Always chases the ball, or never engages.
Usually knows when to go to the ball and when to stay.
Good sense of when to press and when to cover.
U11–U13: Always chases the ball, or always stands off.
Usually chooses correctly between pressing and holding.
Consistently good timing: presses on triggers, covers when needed.

w: Defending against an attacker one-on-one.

U9–U10: Dives in or stands off; rarely stops the attacker.
Stays on their feet and slows the attacker down.
Regularly stops attackers 1v1.
U11–U13: Easily beaten 1v1.
Good body shape; delays and wins a fair share.
Rarely beaten 1v1; shows the attacker where they want.

w: Carrying out defensive duties in team shape.

U9–U10: Doesn't know what to do when we lose the ball.
Knows their basic defensive job.
Does their defensive job fully every time.
U11–U13: Does not know their defensive duties.
Does their defensive duties most of the time.
Carries out the defensive role fully, whatever the position.

w: Controlled intensity in duels and desire to win the ball.

U9–U10: Passive in challenges and games.
Competes for the ball and wants to win.
Fierce but fair competitor in every activity.
U11–U13: Avoids duels; low intensity.
Competes in duels and keeps fighting when losing.
Drives the intensity and wins battles while staying controlled and fair.

w: Concentration on tasks and instructions.

U9–U10: Easily distracted; instructions need repeating.
Concentrates for most of the activity.
Fully focused throughout; follows multi-step instructions.
U11–U13: Switches off in drills and games.
Focused for most of the session or match.
Consistently concentrated, including late in games and when tired.

w: Wanting the ball, trying things, handling mistakes.

U9–U10: Hides from the ball; upset by mistakes.
Asks for the ball and tries again after mistakes.
Always wants the ball; mistakes don't affect them.
U11–U13: Avoids responsibility; one mistake affects the rest of the game.
Wants the ball in most situations; recovers from mistakes.
Demands the ball in big moments; resilient after errors.

w: Communicating, organising and setting standards.

U9–U10: Quiet; doesn't help others.
Encourages teammates.
Others follow them; helps and organises teammates.
U11–U13: Rarely communicates or helps others.
Talks on the pitch and encourages teammates.
Organises others, sets standards and leads by example.

w: Character and presence in the group: positive, respectful, sociable.

U9–U10: Struggles to get along with others or follow group rules.
Positive, respectful and gets on well with the group.
A positive presence who lifts the whole group.
U11–U13: Negative influence; poor reactions to others.
Positive and respectful to teammates, coaches and opponents.
A role model in the group; lifts others on and off the pitch.

w: Response to challenge, mistakes and feedback.

U9–U10: Gives up when something is hard.
Keeps trying when something is difficult; listens to feedback.
Loves a challenge; sees mistakes as part of learning.
U11–U13: Avoids difficult tasks; dismisses feedback.
Accepts challenges and feedback; learns from mistakes.
Seeks challenges and feedback; reflects and visibly improves.

w: Effort and positivity in training and matches.

U9–U10: Effort varies a lot; needs constant encouragement.
Works hard in most activities and stays positive.
Maximum effort every session; a positive influence on others.
U11–U13: Inconsistent effort; negative body language.
Good effort and attitude, including when not starting.
Exemplary effort; responds to setbacks positively.

w: Technical proficiency under pressure.

All ages: Technique breaks down as soon as pressure arrives.
Technique stays clean at match speed under heavy pressure.

w: Decision making and game awareness.

All ages: Rarely aware of what's around them.
Usually aware and makes sensible decisions.
Reads the game and makes the best choice consistently.

w: Leadership, grit and coachability.

All ages: Gives up easily; struggles with feedback.
Keeps going and takes feedback on board.

w: Explosiveness and repeated sprint ability.

All ages: Slow off the mark; can't repeat efforts.
Good short burst; repeats it a few times.
Explosive and repeats sprints all game.
